tagline: Built of honey-coloured sandstone that glows at sunset, Salamanca has one of Europe's oldest universities, two cathedrals and perhaps the most beautiful Plaza Mayor in Spain.
overview: Salamanca, in Castile and León, is home to the University of Salamanca, founded in 1218 and the oldest university in Spain still running. Its golden Villamayor sandstone buildings make the whole old town glow, and it is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

The 18th-century Plaza Mayor, an enclosed baroque square, is the city's living room, especially at night when it is lit up. Salamanca has two cathedrals joined together, the Romanesque Old Cathedral and the Gothic New Cathedral, and their towers can be climbed through the Ieronimus tour.

The university's ornate façade hides a small carved frog on a skull, and spotting it is said to bring luck in exams. The Casa de las Conchas is covered in carved shells, and students fill the city's tapas bars, giving Salamanca a youthful buzz.
